newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end firmer as fears of higher rates wither.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end firmer as fears of higher rates wither.

text.p: Key 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures closed firmer on Tuesday as fears of higher interest rates, which had dampened JGBs since late last week, withered due to the central bank's accommodative credit stance.
"The money market calmed down today given the BOJ's accommodative operation and so did the bond market," said a long-term credit bank dealer.

The Ministry of Finance's (MOF) 10-year bond auction had a limited impact on JGBs as the auction went as well as expected, traders said. The key June futures contract ended up 0.22 at 125.32. Turnover was 46,419 contracts.
The contract recouped an early loss to 124.98 soon after the Bank of Japan (BOJ) refrained from conducting its regular money market operation at 9.20 a.m. (0020 GMT).
The BOJ's inaction represented an accommodative stance, as the money market was in surplus by about 120 billion yen.
JGBs fell sharply on Monday after the BOJ surprised the market by maintaining a neutral stance in its daily operation.
As a result, the key overnight call rate jumped to 0.57 percent, the highest level since the BOJ last cut its discount rate to the current record low 0.5 percent in September 1995.
The recent fall in JGBs started on March 18 when remarks by a senior BOJ official suggested the market had overshot and the MOF said a land liquidity scheme would be announced March 31.
But given a change in the BOJ's stance in its daily operation on Tuesday morning, the key overnight rate stabilised at around 0.53 percent on Tuesday, money traders said.

The key June contract gave up rises in the morning after comments by MOF minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka that the ministry would monitor movements in market interest rates. But traders said they failed to react to it aggressively as they were not sure what Mitsuzuka was implying.
In the cash market, some small-lot buying by investors was detected in medium-term JGBs as a result of a correction after the yield curve flattened recently, traders said.
"Market sentiment has improved quickly since investors' buying blocked a rise in the yield of the key 182nd 10-year bond at 2.4 percent on Monday," the dealer said.
The key bond yield stood at 2.340 percent at 0747 GMT, down 0.005 from Monday's finish. The yield moved between 2.370 and 2.330 percent.
The newly auctioned 10-year JGBs attracted demand mainly from regional investors, traders said.

Despite its record low coupon rate of 2.5 percent, demand for the 10-year bond was consistent from local mutual funds and agricultural financial and semi-governmental financial institutions. These investors are looking for high-liquidity bonds with a price at under par, traders said.
The auction produced a lowest price of 99.90 and an average price of 99.95, both in line with expectations.

The JGB market will keep an eye on the dollar/yen rate after the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting later on Tuesday and Japan's industrial output data on Friday, traders said. -- Risa Maeda Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-33432-8570
